text:
anya: quick heads-up — during our partner logs ingest I found a KMS-wrapped blob referencing privaterelay-prod credentials (looks like an old service key). I pulled minimal details, filing here for triage 
lee: ugh. where in the pipeline? link?
anya: S3 object path: s3://partner-logs/2026/03/20/ingest-privaterelay-blob.log — the blob name matches our old relay SA key wrap id. No plaintext in the log, just ciphertext and an IAM principal id.
marta: do we have evidence the ciphertext was exfiltrated or just stored in partner logs?
anya: only stored in partner logs. Partner says they retained logs for 30d. They gave us a copy for investigation.
jamie: immediate actions: 1) mark key as suspicious, 2) rotate any active service accounts that used that key, 3) audit decrypt requests, 4) ensure partner rotates their copy or deletes.
anya: agreed. I'm proposing a scoped rotation for the relay service keys first, then a full sweep if we see anomalous decrypts.
lee: how old is the key? can we rewrap instead of full rotation? KMS supports rewrap but we need to ensure Vault transit + KMS mapping updates.
marta: rewrap only helps if master keys rotated; but service account tokens that used the prior plaintext still need rotation. safer to rotate the SA and reissue creds.
jamie: checklist I'm starting:
- run KMS audit: gcloud logging read 'resource.type=kms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName:Decrypt' --limit 1000
- list Vault leases for relay: vault list sys/leases/lookup | grep relay
- rotate relay SA: gcloud iam service-accounts keys create --iam-account=relay@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com new-key.json
- update deployments: k8s secret update, restart pods with new key references
- partner: request immediate deletion of logged ciphertext and confirmation
anya: I'll start the KMS audit query and attach results here.
sec-bot: INCIDENT-2026-023 created: sec-542987 (severity: medium). Assigned: eng-security.
oncall: tagging oncall for vault ops — @oncall can you help with rekey/revoke window planning?
oncall: ETA for a maintenance window today 18:30-19:00 PT, but we can do rolling to avoid downtime.
lee: quick question on Vault/KMS integration — some relay tokens are wrapped via GCP KMS with a different key ring. If we rotate the relay SA, will any stored Vault transit ciphertext referencing the old SA break?
marta: the ciphertext is independent of the SA used to encrypt it in Vault transit; but if Vault uses KMS to wrap transit master key, rewrapping may be required. Check Vault's transit key wrapping config: vault read sys/mounts/transit | grep -A3 'wrapping_key'
jamie: for safety, plan: 1) snapshot Vault policies and mounts, 2) export list of secrets that reference relay SA - `vault list secret/relay/` 3) run a staged rotate on non-prod first.
anya: audit output: found 3 decrypt calls in past 60d from partner ingestion project, timestamps show decrypt-from-service-account: partner-ingest@partner-proj. No successful Decrypt from unknown principals. Attaching snippet: `protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail = partner-ingest@partner-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
lee: that's reassuring (no unknown principals). Still we need to reduce blast radius. Proposed minimal plan: rotate relay SA keys + revoke old keys, set a short TTL on new keys, update RBAC so partner cannot request decrypts for our KMS keys, and ask partner to delete logs.
marta: RBAC change: add deny entry on KMS key IAM policy for partner project. We can add a conditional binding to restrict Decrypt to our service accounts only. I'll draft the IAM policy change.
jamie: also add an audit alert: log-based metric on KMS Decrypt where principal != our-relay-sa and trigger PagerDuty if >0 in 1h window.
anya: partner confirmed immediate deletion and is rotating their end. They want a signed confirmation template — can someone draft a short note?
lee: I'll draft and send. Include: deletion path, retention window cleared, sha256 of deleted file (if available), and timestamp.
devops: deployment notes — after new SA key is created, we'll update k8s secret in staging first: `kubectl create secret generic relay-sa --from-file=key.json=new-key.json --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` then restart deployment `kubectl rollout restart deployment/relay`
marta: timeline proposal:
- T+0h: create incident ticket (done)
- T+0.5h: rotate relay SA keys (jamie + devops)
- T+1h: update k8s secrets in staging, smoke test
- T+3h: update production secrets, rolling restart, monitor errors
- T+24h: re-evaluate, run full secret sweep if anomalous decrypts seen
anya: can we add a quick script to find any KMS blob references across logs: `grep -R "projects/.*/locations/.*/keyRings/.*/cryptoKeys/" /mnt/partner-logs | sed -n '1,200p'`
lee: that's ok as a first pass but be careful with partners' data. Do it in the partner-provided copy only.
jamie: I've created a PR with rotation scripts and a checklist: https://git.redwood/infrasec/privaterelay-rotation/pull/12
sec-bot: attached runbook: https://confluence.redwood/security/incident-runbooks#kms-blob-exposure
anya: action owners: jamie (rotate + k8s update), devops (deploy & restart), marta (IAM policy + audit metric), lee (partner comms + deletion confirmation), anya (investigation + postmortem).
marta: IAM draft (short):
```
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
  members:
    - serviceAccount:relay@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# remove partner project service accounts
```
Lee: I'll review and push to infra repo after approval.
oncall: during rotation window I'll standby for rollback. If Vault transit complains about wrapping key, ping me immediately.
anya: thanks everyone. I'll post updates here after rotation. Please ack when done. :thumbsup:
jamie: ack, starting rotation now.
devops: staging updated, relay pods restarted, smoke tests passed (end-to-end message throughput OK).
jamie: prod update in progress; rolling restarts ongoing.
marta: IAM policy applied to KMS key; partner service accounts removed. Logging alert created: KMS-decrypt-unexpected -> PagerDuty.
lee: partner deletion confirmation received and attached to ticket.
anya: closing loop: prod rotation complete, no anomalous decrypts detected, incident downgraded to low. Postmortem will include hardening checklist for partner log scoping and mandatory KMS IAM least privilege.
sec-bot: INCIDENT-2026-023 status changed to resolved.
anya: thanks all — we'll file the postmortem doc and schedule the RBAC hardening RFC next week.
